newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Infrastructure costs weigh on companies - BHP.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Infrastructure costs weigh on companies - BHP.

text.p: High infrastructire costs are hurting Australia businesses, John Prescott managing director of Australia's largest company, the Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd (BHP) said on Wednesday.
Prescott said Australia's electricity prices were around 40 percent abover the world's best practice standards while telecommunications costs were about 80 percent higher.
Addressing the Australia-Israel Chamber of Commerce, Prescott also said rail and waterfront costs were around twice that of the world's best practice.
"Taken collectively those higher costs are 'lead in the saddle bags' of Australia firms," Prescott said.
The impact of the extra costs are substantial, he said.

It costs BHP three to six times as much to transport a tonne of coal from one of its Queensland mines by a government run railroad than it does for BHP to ship the same amount of iron ore from the remote Pilbara region of Western Australia to Port Hedland via BHP's own rail system, despite being twice the distance, Prescott said.
"We estimate that improved competition could give rise to cost savings to BHP Minerals in the order of A$300 million per year in Queensland alone," Prescott said.
Similar burdens are being imposed in many other areas including resource title, security, taxation issues and compliance costs, Prescott said.
